2. Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat Programme
 Bharat has diverse languages, cuisines, music, dance, theatre, movies
 and films, handicrafts, sports, literature, festivals, paintings, sculptures,
 etc. The Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat programme aims to enhance
 interaction and promote mutual understanding between people of
 different states/UTs through the concept of state/UT pairing. This is to
 celebrate the unity in diversity and strengthen the emotional bonds
 between its citizens. The vision is to enable people to develop a sense
 of common identity by sharing best practices and experiences. The
 programme aims to contribute to nation building by highlighting the
 inter-connectedness between various cultures and traditions.

Up in the air
 See the kites fly,
 Like coloured birds
 In the wind-whipped sky.

I wish I were small
 And light as air,
 I would climb on a kite
 And sail up there.

Then I would drift upon
 The paper wings,
 And hear the songs
 That the wild wind sings.

What fun it would be
 To look right down,
 Over the park
 And the rooftops of town.

The people below
 Would stand and stare,
 And wish they were me
 High, high in the air.

Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat Programme

The Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat programme is conducted to know that we all belong to one nation and share a bond. It aims to celebrate unity in diversity by enhancing interaction between people of different states or UTs through state/UT pairing.

Aipan Folk Art

Aipan is a folk art form made by women in families using white rice flour paste on brick-red walls coloured with geru. The designs are beautiful, mathematical, and based on cultural traditions and observations of nature.

Dhokra Metal Craft

The Dhokra craft is a 4000-year-old metal craft where a figure is made with clay, covered with wax, carved with details, then covered with more clay and fired. The wax melts and comes out of small openings when brass scrap is poured into the empty space.

Coconut Shell Craft

In coconut shell craft, a brown coconut shell is cleaned, smoothed, given a shape, fixed with a base, polished to shine, and used to make household things like bowls and jewellery. It is a biodegradable craft.

Kondapalli Toys

The Kondapalli art involves carving soft wood from hills, joining pieces with tamarind seed powder and sawdust paste, adding details, and finishing with vegetable dyes or enamel paints. These toys are based on folk stories, animals, birds, rural life, etc.

Art Order of Making

The order of making art forms is shown by specific words: to begin, first, then, after that, next, finally, at last. For example, in Dhokra, a figure is made with clay, then covered with wax, carved, and finally fired.

Present Tense Grammar

When children from different states speak about their art forms, they use the first form of the verb to show something that happens regularly. This is called the present tense, where -s/-es is used with he/she/it.

Gakkad Bharta Ingredients

To make gakkad bharta, balls of dough are made and cooked on high heat. Then brinjal and tomatoes are added, garnished with onions, coriander, green chillies, and salt. Finally, crumbled gakkad is served with ghee.

Madhubani Painting

Madhubani painting is a traditional art form from Bihar where artists use natural colours like haldi (yellow), leaves (green), red flowers/geru/sindoor (red), flowers (orange), and neel/indigo powder (blue) to paint on walls.

Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat Programme

The Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat programme is conducted to know that we all belong to one nation and share a bond. It aims to celebrate unity in diversity by enhancing interaction between people of different states or UTs through state/UT pairing.

Aipan Folk Art

Aipan is a folk art form made by women in families using white rice flour paste on brick-red walls coloured with geru. The designs are beautiful, mathematical, and based on cultural traditions and observations of nature.

Dhokra Metal Craft

The Dhokra craft is a 4000-year-old metal craft where a figure is made with clay, covered with wax, carved with details, then covered with more clay and fired. The wax melts and comes out of small openings when brass scrap is poured into the empty space.

Coconut Shell Craft

In coconut shell craft, a brown coconut shell is cleaned, smoothed, given a shape, fixed with a base, polished to shine, and used to make household things like bowls and jewellery. It is a biodegradable craft.

Kondapalli Toys

The Kondapalli art involves carving soft wood from hills, joining pieces with tamarind seed powder and sawdust paste, adding details, and finishing with vegetable dyes or enamel paints. These toys are based on folk stories, animals, birds, rural life, etc.

Art Order of Making

The order of making art forms is shown by specific words: to begin, first, then, after that, next, finally, at last. For example, in Dhokra, a figure is made with clay, then covered with wax, carved, and finally fired.

Present Tense Grammar

When children from different states speak about their art forms, they use the first form of the verb to show something that happens regularly. This is called the present tense, where -s/-es is used with he/she/it.

Gakkad Bharta Ingredients

To make gakkad bharta, balls of dough are made and cooked on high heat. Then brinjal and tomatoes are added, garnished with onions, coriander, green chillies, and salt. Finally, crumbled gakkad is served with ghee.

Madhubani Painting

Madhubani painting is a traditional art form from Bihar where artists use natural colours like haldi (yellow), leaves (green), red flowers/geru/sindoor (red), flowers (orange), and neel/indigo powder (blue) to paint on walls.
